newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Wharf Cable TV to post lower losses - HK paper.
newsitem.headline: Wharf Cable TV to post lower losses - HK paper.

text.p: Wharf Cable Ltd, the cable television unit of Wharf (Holdings) Ltd, will post an operating loss of an estimated HK$400 million in calendar 1996, the Hong Kong Economic Journal said on Friday.

Annual operating costs for the company were HK$1.0 billion, with revenue estimated at HK$600 million for this year and operating losses at about HK$400 million, the newspaper quoted Wharf Cable chairman Stephen Ng as saying.

Ng forecast operating losses would continue to narrow to less than HK$200 million in 1997, adding that a profit was expected in 1998. Wharf Cable recorded a loss of HK$824 million in 1995, the newspaper said.
Ng said the number of subscribers had risen to more than 300,000 by December from between 170,000 and 180,000 during the same period last year.
Total investment exceeded HK$6.0 billion, higher than the planned HK$5.0 billion, said Ng, who is also managing director of Wharf (Holdings).
About 80 percent of Wharf Cable's revenues come from monthly subscription fees, with the remainder from movie channels, the newspaper said.
